subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
lesson: Lesson 4: WOW! Book Club – A diary
outcomes: Know the features of a diary entry.
Put the events of Khalid’s cyclone story in order.
Use phrasal verbs with get: under, out, into, down, up, onto.

tf.s: A diary is usually written in the first person.
tf.why: Yes, the writer uses I and we.

tf.s: A diary is usually very formal.
A diary tells us about the writer’s life and feelings.
tf.why: Great! Diaries share the writer’s life and feelings.

tf.s: Khalid’s frightening experience was a cyclone.
Khalid got up late because he was tired.
tf.why: He got up early because the big storm woke him up.

tf.s: The family went to the dining room because it was the safest place in the house.
tf.why: Correct! The dining room was the safest place.

tf.s: In the morning, the cyclone was still very strong.
tf.why: In the morning the rain stopped and the cyclone was over.

tf.s: In an earthquake, you should get onto a table.
tf.why: You should get under a table.

tf.s: The harbour flooded before the family went to the dining room.
tf.why: Yes, the harbour flooded first, then they went to the dining room.

tf.s: Khalid’s dad told him to worry a lot.
tf.why: His dad said not to worry.

boxes.q: Is a diary usually formal or informal?
boxes.why: Diaries are personal, so they are informal.

boxes.q: Why did Khalid get up early?
o: The big storm woke him up.

boxes.q: Where did the family go to be safe?
boxes.why: The dining room was the safest place.
The rain stopped and the cyclone was over.

boxes.q: If there’s an earthquake, get ___ a table.
boxes.why: Under a table keeps you safe.

boxes.q: My father used a ladder to get ___ the roof.
boxes.why: We get onto a high surface like a roof.
Get out of means leave a place.

boxes.q: We got ___ the car and drove away.
A diary uses “I” and “we”. This is called…
boxes.why: I and we are first person.
The harbour flooded in the storm.

hunt.q: The safest room in the house
A diary is written in the…

mcq.q: Which is a feature of a diary?
o: It is about the writer’s life and feelings.
It is written in the third person.
It has no dates or events.
mcq.why: A diary is personal and informal.

o: He got lost in the desert.

mcq.why: His dad told him not to worry.

mcq.q: Why did the family go to the dining room?
o: It was the safest place in the house.
mcq.why: They went there to be safe.

mcq.q: Choose the correct phrasal verb: “The baby cat is on the tree. Can you help it get ___?”
mcq.why: Get down means come down from a high place.

o: The bus is here. Let’s get onto it.
The bus is here. Let’s get under it.
The bus is here. Let’s get out it.
The bus is here. Let’s get down it.

mcq.q: Which sentence sounds like a diary entry?
o: Today I woke up early and felt really scared.
Cyclones are storms with strong winds.
Dear Sir, I am writing to complain.
Turn left at the end of the road.
mcq.why: A diary uses I and talks about feelings.

mcq.q: Which order of events is correct?
o: woke up early → harbour flooded → dining room → rain stopped
rain stopped → woke up early → harbour flooded → dining room
dining room → woke up early → rain stopped → harbour flooded
harbour flooded → rain stopped → woke up early → dining room
mcq.why: This follows the story from start to end.

mcq.q: How did Khalid probably feel during the cyclone?
mcq.why: The diary is about a frightening experience.

mcq.q: Why do people write about feelings in a diary?
o: A diary is personal, about the writer’s own life.
A diary is a science report.
A diary is for selling things.
mcq.why: Diaries share personal experiences and feelings.
